name_en: Ren (humaneness)
one_line_en: The virtue of treating others as fully human, which Confucius made the centre of the good life.

name_en: Wu wei (non-action)
one_line_en: The best ruler and the best way act by not forcing; order arises when interference stops.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Daodejing 37 (Q_003, idea_link IL_006), re-found at its locator this session (2026-09-13) by a programmatic check of the quoted English against the fetched source (ctext.org/dao-de-jing/ens). Range -400/-250 = W_DAODEJING's composition window (Guodian c. -300, Mawangdui c. -200; Loewe 1993 as cited on that row).

name_en: The Middle Way / conditioned arising
one_line_en: Suffering has causes and can be ended by a path that avoids both indulgence and self-torture.
first_attestation_basis: Originated by P_BUDDHA (IL_008); first stated in its own words at SN 56.11 (Q_074, IL_139), re-found at its locator this session (2026-09-13) by a programmatic check of the quoted English against the fetched source (bilara-data sn56.11 translation JSON), and summarised in DN 16's last words (Q_005, IL_009; not re-read this session; this basis rests on the merged rows named). The range dates the Buddha's teaching, not the texts: W_SN56_11 and W_DN16 are -400/-100. Range -471/-100, derived in the r4-5 update below; the -450/-380 first given here, which was not the teaching-life constant round02_batchB §5.3 states (-471/-380), is superseded. r4-5 UPDATE (2026-09-15), residue 2 and ruling L-60's idea-range convention: the range -450/-380 is replaced by -471/-100. (1) THE CONSTANT: the Buddha-frame teaching-life constant is -471/-380, as round02_batchB section 5.3 defines it; -450 had no derivation anywhere in the corpus. Derivation: P_BUDDHA's short-chronology birth range -500/-460 and death range -420/-380; he went forth at twenty-nine (DN 16, dn16:5.27.5-6, 'I was twenty-nine years of age, Subhadda, when I went forth') and was eighty at the end (dn16:2.25.10, 'I'm currently eighty years old'), both segments read this session in suttacentral/bilara-data (published branch, Sujato translation and Mahasangiti root), so everything he did as a renouncer falls between the earliest going-forth (-500 + 29 = -471) and the latest death (-380). (2) THE RANGE: under L-60 a first-attestation range may open at the earliest sourced utterance its attesting text reports, here the teaching life's floor -471 for the utterance SN 56.11 (Q_074, IL_139) reports, and closes at the attesting work's own ceiling: W_SN56_11 is -400/-100, so the close is -100, not -380. The originating passage was not re-read this session; this basis rests on the merged rows named.

name_en: Ahimsa (non-harm)
one_line_en: Harming any living being is wrong; systematised by the Jains and adopted by Buddhism. First attested here in the oldest stratum of the Jain canon, generations after Mahavira.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Acaranga 1.4.1.1 (Q_014, idea_link IL_026); not re-read this session; this basis rests on the merged rows named (sacred-texts.com refused this session and the archive.org file name tried returned 404). Range -400/-200 = W_ACARANGA's composition window (oldest stratum of the Jain canon; Dundas as cited on that row). The idea is linked to P_MAHAVIRA as originator (IL_010), generations earlier than the text.

name_en: Individual moral responsibility
one_line_en: Each person answers for their own deeds, not for their fathers' — Ezekiel's break with collective guilt.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Ezekiel 18:20 (Q_006, idea_link IL_012), re-read at its locator this session through the Sefaria API (JPS 1917 and Tanach with Text Only, both Public Domain). Range -593/-571 is the span of the book's dated oracles as W_EZEKIEL's basis states it ('Dated oracles 593-571'), not the work's full window (-593/-540), which allows for later editorial layers.

name_en: Exclusive monotheism
one_line_en: There is one God and no other, who governs all nations — first stated flatly in Second Isaiah.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Isaiah 45:5 (Q_007, idea_link IL_014), re-read at its locator this session through the Sefaria API. Range -550/-539 = W_ISAIAH_40_55's composition window (references to Cyrus as conqueror-liberator), which ends at the fall of Babylon in October 539 by the work's own basis.

name_en: Asha versus Druj (truth against the Lie)
one_line_en: The cosmos and the state are a contest between truth-order and the Lie; each person must choose.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Yasna 30.3 (Q_009, idea_link IL_016), re-read this session in SBE 31 (archive.org sbe31zendavestapart3_202002; sacred-texts refused), and developed at Behistun DB §55 (Q_008, IL_017), re-read this session in Tolman 1908. Lower bound -1200 = W_GATHAS's lower bound (linguistic dating); upper bound -518 = the end of W_BEHISTUN's window, the first securely dated attestation. The range therefore runs from the earliest date the Gathas may have to the latest date by which the idea is certainly in writing.

name_en: Logos
one_line_en: A single rational principle (logos) underlies all change.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Heraclitus DK B50 = Burnet fr. 1 (Q_010, idea_link IL_019); not re-read this session; this basis rests on the merged rows named (the Wikisource page names tried returned 404). Range -505/-480 = W_HERACLITUS_FR's composition window.

name_en: Isonomia / demokratia (equality before the law; rule of the people)
one_line_en: Political membership defined by citizenship rather than birth, and decisions by the assembled many.
first_attestation_basis: No passage row originates this idea. The range begins with an event: -508 is the lower bound of E_GR_002, Cleisthenes' reforms (enacts, IL_020). It ends at -430, the upper bound of E_GR_004, Pericles' funeral oration, whose text is Q_012 (Thucydides 2.37.1, develops, IL_022, re-read this session in the MIT Crawley text). The earliest text linked is Herodotus 3.80.6 (Q_011, IL_021, re-read this session), inside W_HERODOTUS -440/-420. So the range dates the institution and its classic description, not a first written attestation; that difference from the batch B practice is flagged to the lead.

name_en: The examined life
one_line_en: A life not subjected to questioning is not worth living; philosophy as a personal duty.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Apology 38a (Q_013, idea_link IL_024), re-found at its locator this session (2026-09-13) by a programmatic check of the quoted English against the fetched source (Fowler, PerseusDL tlg0059.tlg002). Upper bound -380 = W_APOLOGY's composition ceiling (the full-window equation held until the lower bound was rederived, 2026-10-12, below) (written within a generation of the trial). Lower bound -400 (2026-10-12): the idea's anchor is the trial's utterance (Apology 38a), and the trial (E_GR_005) is -400/-399 on Diogenes Laertius 2.44 (Ol. 95.1), so the idea opens at the trial's earliest year; it touches the slice's inclusive -400 end.

name_en: Nomos and physis (custom against nature)
one_line_en: Are the rules people live by grounded in nature, or are they only local custom that could have been otherwise? The question that made Greek ethics an argument.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Herodotus 3.38.4 (Q_017, idea_link IL_027), re-found at its locator this session (2026-09-13) by a programmatic check of the quoted English against the fetched source (PerseusDL Godley); W_HERODOTUS is -440/-420. name_en: Arete (excellence) and what a city should honour
one_line_en: Excellence — and the dispute over what kind of excellence a community should reward: physical prowess, birth, or thought.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Xenophanes DK 21 B2 (Q_028, idea_link IL_034); not re-read this session; this basis rests on the merged rows named (the Wikisource page names tried returned 404). Range -545/-475 = W_XENOPHANES_FR's composition window.

name_en: Hubris and the levelling of greatness
one_line_en: Whatever rises too high is struck down: the god will not let anything but himself think big. The Greek explanation of why empires fall.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Herodotus 7.10ε (Q_016, idea_link IL_036), re-found at its locator this session (2026-09-13) by a programmatic check of the quoted English against the fetched source (PerseusDL Godley). Range -440/-420 = W_HERODOTUS's composition window.

name_en: Atomism
one_line_en: Everything that exists is uncuttable particles moving in empty space; everything else is how they happen to be arranged.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Diogenes Laertius 9.45 = DK 68 A1 (Q_026, idea_link IL_039), re-found at its locator this session (2026-09-13) by a programmatic check of the quoted English against the fetched source (PerseusDL Hicks). Range -440/-380 = W_DEMOCRITUS_FR's composition window, i.e. Democritus's working life; the passage itself is a third-century CE testimonium, as its note says.

name_en: Man the measure (sophistic relativism)
one_line_en: The human being is the measure of what is and what is not — so there is no appeal beyond human judgement, and every question has two sides.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Diogenes Laertius 9.51 = DK 80 B1 (Q_024, idea_link IL_041), re-found at its locator this session (2026-09-13) by a programmatic check of the quoted English against the fetched source (PerseusDL Hicks). name_en: Dike (justice) as the order of things
one_line_en: Justice as a settlement that holds the world together: the same word for a court's award and for the balance the cosmos keeps.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Anaximander DK 12 B1 (Q_027, idea_link IL_045); not re-read this session; this basis rests on the merged rows named (the Wikisource page names tried returned 404). Range -560/-546 = W_ANAXIMANDER_FR's composition window.

name_en: Rule by published law
one_line_en: Cast the penal code where anyone can read it, so that people are governed by known rules instead of by the judgement of their superiors.

name_en: Tianming (Heaven's mandate and Heaven's way)
one_line_en: Heaven's charge to rule, which can be lost — and, in the Chunqiu-period sources, an impersonal regularity that brings down whatever is full.

name_en: Covenant, and a covenant that could be rewritten
one_line_en: The bond between a people and its God understood as an agreement with terms - which means it can be broken, and can be made again on different terms.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Jeremiah 31:31-33 (Q_062, idea_link IL_075): ‘a NEW covenant, not according to the covenant made with their fathers, with the law put in their inward parts.’ The idea of covenant is older than the slice; what is new, and what this attestation records, is a covenant deliberately rewritten. Range -627/-550 = W_JEREMIAH's own composition window (the book dates its oracles by Judahite/Babylonian regnal years, read at their locators in r2-5).

name_en: The anointed one (mashiach), given to a foreigner
one_line_en: The title of Israel's own kings - the anointed - applied by a prophet to a Persian conqueror who had never heard of the god who used it.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Isaiah 45:1 (Q_058, idea_link IL_079): 'thus saith the LORD to His anointed, to Cyrus.' Range -550/-539 = W_ISAIAH_40_55's composition window, the envelope of the text in which the word is used; how its end-year came to be -539 follows. ALIGNED 2026-09-13 (Sophia r3-5, residue item 3, L-53): the range previously ended at -539, one year short of the work's -538. The -539 followed E_IL_024's reading of the content (the oracles speak of gates still to be opened, so before the fall of Babylon, which E_PE_001 and Parker & Dubberstein 1942 p. 11 date to October 539). But an idea's first attestation is a claim about the text, and this corpus gives Isaiah 40-55's other ideas (I_MONOTHEISM, I_SERVANT) the full work window; a prophecy may also postdate what it foretells. Aligning widens the range by a year, which is the permitted direction; narrowing W_ISAIAH_40_55 to -539 would not be. A related observation, not acted on: W_ISAIAH_40_55's own composition_basis says 'between Cyrus's rise and the fall of Babylon', which is 539, while its number is -538. r3-mergeB UPDATE (2026-09-13), ruling L-59(6)/rider (d): follows W_ISAIAH_40_55's window end, itself realigned this same commit series to -539 (its own basis text names 'the fall of Babylon', October 539) -- so -550/-539, not the -550/-538 the r3-5 substitution set.

name_en: A God who is not tied to a building or a country
one_line_en: Deported and told they had lost everything, the Judeans were told instead that God had gone with them and been a small sanctuary in the countries where they had come - the beginning of a religion that can travel.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Ezekiel 11:16 (Q_053, idea_link IL_083): ‘yet have I been to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they are come.’ Range -597/-571 follows the batch's own Ezekiel year-stamp conversion (docs/changes/round02_batchB.md §5.1: captivity-year N -> Julian year, anchored to Jehoiachin's 597 deportation, ABC 5).

name_en: The servant who carries what belongs to others
one_line_en: A figure who is wounded for other people's wrongs and by whose bruises they are healed - suffering read as something borne on behalf of others rather than deserved.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Isaiah 53:4-5 (Q_060, idea_link IL_089): ‘surely our diseases he did bear; he was wounded because of our transgressions.’ Range -550/-539 = W_ISAIAH_40_55's own composition window, which ends at the fall of Babylon in October 539 by the work's own basis.

name_en: A book read aloud as the constitution of a community
one_line_en: A people organised not around a king or a temple but around a text read out in public, translated and explained so that everyone present could follow it.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Nehemiah 8:8 (Q_065, idea_link IL_092): ‘they read in the book distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.’ Range -445/-385 holds open both the Artaxerxes I and II readings of Nehemiah's dating (ruling L-20, reliability=low; docs/changes/round02_batchB.md §5.2).

name_en: The sabbath as a portable sign
one_line_en: A day kept every seventh day, named as the sign between God and this people - an observance that needs no land, no temple and no priest, and so survives losing all three.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Ezekiel 20:12 (Q_055, idea_link IL_096): ‘I gave them My sabbaths, to be a sign between Me and them.’ Range -591/-571 follows the batch's own Ezekiel year-stamp conversion (docs/changes/round02_batchB.md §5.1).

name_en: Karma: a person is made by what they do
one_line_en: Action has moral consequences that outlast the action and shape what a being becomes - stated first as a secret worth taking outside the hall to discuss, and later as the plain answer to why people are born unequal.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Brihadaranyaka Upanishad III, 2, 13 (Q_083, idea_link IL_103): ‘what they said was karman, that a man becomes good by good work,’ a teaching the text itself frames as too dangerous to discuss in a full hall. r4-9 CORRECTION (2026-09-20), against L-60's closing rule: the range is now the attesting work's own composition range, -1000/-600, the value W_BRIHADARANYAKA itself carries. It CLOSES at -600 because that is the attesting work's own ceiling — Mueller, SBE 1, Introduction p. lxvii: the ancient Upanishads ‘must be, if we follow the chronology which at present is commonly … received by Sanskrit scholars, older than 600 B.C., i.e. anterior to the rise of Buddhism.’ The previous -400 was W_MN135's composition FLOOR, and MN 135 (Q_077, IL_104) is a `develops` link, not the originating attestation, so it could not set this row's ceiling. It OPENS at -1000 because no sourced utterance anchor exists: IL_105 records that Yajnavalkya is traditional and that no date attaches to him, so — unlike the five Buddha-teaching rows, whose anchor is the teaching life at -471 (L-60, L-70(2), L-71(4)) — the open end falls back to the attesting work's own floor. Mueller p. lxvi fixes the Mantra period, in which ‘the first germs of Upanishad doctrines’ lie, ‘provisionally … between 1000 and 800 B.C.’; the previous -800 silently took the later end of that bracket while citing the p. lxvii sentence, which does not yield it. Read at their locators on 2026-09-20, this session: Q_083 in the archive.org OCR of SBE 15 (item upanishads02ml, upanishads02ml_djvu.txt, 844,033 bytes, fetched from node ia800706.us.archive.org because archive.org's own /download redirect host did not resolve this session), the text reading ‘what they said was karman (work), what they praised was karman, viz. that a man becomes good by good work, and bad by bad w^ork’ — the OCR corruption Q_083's note already records; and SBE 1, Introduction pp. lxvi-lxvii in item upanishads01mluoft (upanishads01mluoft_djvu.txt, 846,330 bytes, node ia600902.us.archive.org), the byte count matching the one SRC_SBE01's note records. CONSEQUENCE, recorded and not repaired: the corrected range now lies wholly before the pilot slice (600-400 BCE), abutting it at -600. The straddle flagged in docs/changes/round02_batchB.md §5.4 widens; the idea's presence inside the slice is carried by its in-slice `develops` link to MN 135, not by this range.

name_en: Samsara: wandering on through birth after birth
one_line_en: Life understood as one link in a chain of births that keeps going - the shared premise that Indian teachers of every school argued inside, and disagreed only about how, or whether, to get out of.
first_attestation_basis: First attested in the same exchange as I_KARMA, Brihadaranyaka III, 2, 13 (Q_083, idea_link IL_108, `originates`): what a person becomes by good and bad work presupposes a becoming that outlasts the person. r4-9 CORRECTION (2026-09-20), against L-60's closing rule: the range is now the attesting work's own composition range, -1000/-600, identical to I_KARMA's because the originating attestation is the same passage in the same work. The previous -800/-380 failed the rule at both ends and more badly than I_KARMA's. Its late end followed Q_079 (DN 2's report of the ascetic Gosala, idea_link IL_109), which is a `develops` link and not the originating attestation; and -380 is not even that work's ceiling — W_DN2's composition range is -400/-100 — so the number belonged to the Buddha's death range rather than to any work cited here. one_line_en: Nothing a person is made of is the self, and the argument is from control: if any of it were yours, you could tell it what to be, and you cannot.

name_en: The order as a self-governing community with its own law
one_line_en: A community of renouncers that meets, decides in common and holds property in common, governed by rules it recites together - modelled, on the canon's own account, on the assembly practice of a north Indian republic.

name_en: King by the favour of the god
one_line_en: A king rules because a god chose him and helps him - so a rebel is not a rival but a liar against the order the god set up.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Behistun DB §5 (Q_088, idea_link IL_142): 'By the grace of Ahura Mazda I am king; Ahura Mazda gave me the kingdom.' Range -520/-518 = W_BEHISTUN's composition window (merged row). name_original is Tolman's transliteration of the formula as the OCR prints it (diacritics lost), read this session in col. I. The Cyrus Cylinder (-539/-530) makes Marduk choose Cyrus (Q_099), which is earlier; it is linked as a parallel written in Akkadian for Babylon, not as this Old Persian formula's first attestation. NAME_ORIGINAL ALIGNED 2026-10-13 (Sophia r12-1b): the sentence above was true as read on its date, before the clean Old Persian of SRC_ARIO was in this corpus. name_original is now ARIo's normalised transcription of the formula as Q_088 quotes it, read 2026-10-13 in SRC_ARIO's Oracc export (ario.zip, 2,689,695 bytes; corpusjson/Q007134.json, refs Q007134.12.6-7, DB 'Persian i 11'): 'vašnā A.uramazdāha', whose first word the edition restores in part (Q_088's note lists it).

name_en: One king's law over many peoples
one_line_en: Peoples with their own gods, languages and customs are held together not by one religion but by one royal law they are all expected to keep.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Behistun DB §8 (Q_089, idea_link IL_148): 'by the grace of Ahura Mazda these countries respected my laws', where 'laws' is Old Persian data (Tolman's vocabulary s.v. data, read this session). Range -520/-518 = W_BEHISTUN's composition window (merged row).

name_en: Rule by rectitude: a king who says he lied to no one
one_line_en: The god helped the king, the king says, because he was no liar and no wrongdoer and did not oppress those beneath him - kingship with a moral test attached to it.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Behistun DB §63 (Q_092, idea_link IL_154). Range -520/-518 = W_BEHISTUN's composition window (merged row). The rendering of the people the king did not oppress is marked doubtful by the translator himself (Q_092 note). name_original left blank: the Old Persian of this paragraph was not read at a clean locator this session. IV §13, both scans, re-read 2026-10-13). None of the three words is restored by the edition.

name_en: Gods and deported peoples sent home
one_line_en: A conqueror presents himself not as a destroyer but as the restorer who sends every city's gods back to their temples and every deported people back to its home.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at the Cyrus Cylinder line 32 (Q_098, idea_link IL_157). Range -539/-530 = W_CYRUS_CYLINDER's composition window: after Cyrus's entry into Babylon in October 539 and before his death reported in August 530 (Parker & Dubberstein 1942 pp. 11-12, read this session).

name_en: The god who created happiness for humankind
one_line_en: One great god made earth, sky and people - and made happiness for people too; the king is the one he appointed to keep it.
first_attestation_basis: First attested in Darius's inscriptions: Suez stela c §1 (Q_094, idea_link IL_162) and Naqsh-i Rustam a §1 (Q_095), both undated within Darius's reign; range -522/-486 = that reign per Parker & Dubberstein 1942 pp. 13-14 (read this session), the composition window of both works. Xerxes repeats the formula (Q_097, W_XPA -486/-465). name_original is the word Tolman translates 'welfare', as the OCR of his transliteration prints it ('siyatim', accusative; diacritics lost) in NRa §1. name_en: The Judge's Bridge: the soul answers for its choice
one_line_en: At the Judge's Bridge each soul's choice is settled: the prophet will lead those who stood with him on to it, and the evil-doers who come there will dwell in the Lie's abode for ever.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Yasna 46.10-11 (Q_101, idea_link IL_166). Range -1200/-550 = W_GATHAS's composition window (merged row), which holds open both the linguistic dating and the traditional one; reliability of the link is low for that reason, as for I_ASHA's IL_016. The range straddles the 600 boundary of the pilot slice and is not wholly outside it (L-51(3)). ONE-LINE RE-SAID 2026-10-13 (Sophia r12-1b): the one-line follows only words Mills prints as the Gathic line (Y. 46.10, 'forth to the Judge’s Bridge (itself) with all of them shall I lead on'; 46.11, 'and in the Lie’s abode for ever shall their habitation be'). It no longer uses 'those who followed the Lie miss their path and fall', which it carried until 2026-10-13: 'these shall miss their path and fall' sits inside the long parenthesis that Mills's footnote 7 marks as 'Inserted to shed light on the last line; so the later Parsism' (re-read 2026-10-13 in archive.org item sbe31zendavestapart3_202002, 859,507 bytes; Q_101's note records the same).

name_en: The people as the root of the state
one_line_en: Rulers exist for the people, not the people for the ruler: Heaven sets up a ruler to shepherd them, and one who ruins them may be removed.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Zuozhuan, 襄公十四年 傳 (Q_113, idea_link IL_170), read this session at zh.wikisource.org page 春秋左氏傳/襄公 (revision 9172568, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): Shi Kuang's answer to the marquis of Jin, 天生民而立之君．使司牧之 ... 天之愛民甚矣．豈其使一人肆於民上. The lower bound -559 is the year of the reported speech, NOT the date of the text (the I_LI precedent: -517 for a speech reported in the Zuozhuan); the upper bound -300 is W_ZUOZHUAN's own composition ceiling, as I_LI's is. Duke-year to BCE conversion per calendars.csv CAL_LU, anchored on this dataset's own rows (Zhao 6 = -536 at E_CN_008, so Zhao 1 = -541; Ai 14 = -481 at E_CN_023, so Ai 1 = -494; Ding 1 = -509) and carried back by the reign lengths the edition's own year headers give, counted this session: 僖公 33, 文公 18, 宣公 18, 成公 18, 襄公 31 (so Xi 1 = -659, Wen 1 = -626, Xuan 1 = -608, Cheng 1 = -590, Xiang 1 = -572); the chain closes on both anchors. An earlier witness to the people's benefit as the test of a ruler's choice (文公十三年 傳, 苟利於民, = -614) was read at r8-3 and is not re-read or used here. NOT ANCHORED in 尚書 五子之歌's 民惟邦本 (L-105(6)): that chapter was re-read this session at zh.wikisource.org page 尚書/五子之歌 (revision 2616187, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session) — its header names 梅賾 (noauthor), marks the chapter （僞）, and gives its origin as 古文尚書, the forged old-text Shangshu. THE NAME: 民本 is the conventional modern label for this family of ideas, not a phrase of the anchoring passage; it is recorded as the label, and the CJK check accounts for it in CHANGES.md.

name_en: Promoting the worthy
one_line_en: Office should go to ability, not birth: raise the capable even from farm and workshop, and put the incapable down.
first_attestation_basis: First attested at Mozi, 尚賢上第八 (Q_114, idea_link IL_173), read this session at zh.wikisource.org page 墨子閒詁/卷二 (revision 853986, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 列德而尚賢，雖在農與工肆之人，有能則舉之 and 夫尚賢者，政之本也. Range = W_MOZI's composition range (-430/-200), the I_JIANAI precedent (r3-mergeB, L-59/rider (c)): the Mozi chapters cannot be dated more finely than the work from any source read. The range straddles the 600-400 slice's lower boundary.

name_en: Rule by law (fa)
one_line_en: Govern by public, uniform law backed by certain reward and punishment, applied to every rank alike, rather than by the ruler's discretion or the example of the former kings.
first_attestation_basis: Anchor: 商君書 賞刑第十七 (Q_122, IL_181 originates), read at zh.wikisource.org page 商君書/卷四 (revision 1741809, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): 所謂壹刑者，刑無等級。自卿相將軍以至大夫庶人，有不從王令，犯國禁，亂上制者，罪死不赦。 The range is the window in which the sources read this session place the first written statement of the doctrine. LOWER BOUND -359, the year Shiji 5 gives for Shang Yang's first laws (E_CN_051): the school book that carries the anchor cannot be earlier than the reforms it argues for. UPPER BOUND -233, by which year the doctrine is certainly attested in writing: Han Fei's 五蠹 (Q_124: 以法爲教) is one of the two chapters Shiji 63 says the king of Qin had read before Han Fei came to Qin, and Han Fei died in -233 (Shiji 6; E_CN_059); 五蠹 itself says books of Shang's laws were kept in every household (藏商、管之法者家有之). THE ANCHOR'S OWN DATE IS NOT FIXED within the window: the book of Lord Shang is a school compilation (W_SHANGJUNSHU), one chapter of which postdates -260. The I_JIANAI precedent (an idea anchored in a school compilation takes the window the evidence allows), narrowed at the top by the 五蠹 attestation. Develops I_XINGSHU (IL_190): the sixth-century publication of law (Zheng 536, Jin 513) becomes a theory of the state. Range wholly after the 600-400 slice; R_CN by D-20.

name_en: Great unity (da yitong)
one_line_en: The world should be one realm under a single sovereign order, not a balance of rival states.
first_attestation_basis: Anchor: Mencius 1A6 (Q_119, IL_193 originates), read at zh.wikisource.org page 孟子/梁惠王上 (revision 2642991, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session): asked how the world will be settled, Mencius answers 定於一, 'by unity', and that the one who has no taste for killing will unify it. The range is the reign of King Xiang of Liang, to whom the answer is given, on Shiji 15's chronology (魏襄王元年 at the line labelled 334, 魏哀王元年 at 318), read at zh.wikisource.org page 史記/卷015 (revision 2607002, fetched whole via action=raw on 2026-10-04, this session); that chronology is in tension with the Mencius's own text (E_CN_055.dating_basis), which is why the range is the whole reign and not a year. THIN DATING, STATED: the NAME 大一統 is not Mencius's. It is the Gongyang commentary's (Q_130, IL_194 develops: 何言乎王正月？大一統也), and that text was written down in the Han, under Emperor Jing (-156/-141), on the account the index note to 春秋公羊傳註疏 quotes from a Tang subcommentary (W_GONGYANG). The idea is dated by its earliest statement in this dataset and the name by its text, a century and a half apart; this row says so rather than dating the idea by the later name or the name by the earlier idea. r8-3 drafted Mencius as a 'develops' link; making him the anchor is this batch's change, argued in CHANGES.md. The unification of 221 enacts it (IL_195). Range wholly after the 600-400 slice; R_CN by D-20.
